_comment: FOR THE CUSTOMER, not applied by this repo.
The permissions policy for the role named in hosted-zones.json under
roles.external_dns. Templated from a working deployment, so this is what
the role actually needs rather than a guess.
Its trust policy is the separate example-external-dns-pod-identity-trust.json
-- EKS Pod Identity, not a cross-account assume, because external-dns runs
inside the cluster.
ALSO TAG THIS ROLE  EKSManager = PassRole
Without that tag the pod identity association for it cannot be created.
BOTH ZONES, on purpose. Replace PUBLIC_ZONE_ID and PRIVATE_ZONE_ID with the
two hosted zone ids for this environment. Under split-horizon DNS the two
zones carry the SAME name, and a cluster publishes the same hostname into
both: the public zone so the name resolves from outside, the private zone so
an internal load balancer is reachable by name from inside the VPC.
Scoping this role to the private zone alone leaves the public record
unpublished.
Unlike cert_manager this role genuinely writes A and CNAME records -- that
is its whole job -- so it cannot be constrained by record type. It is
scoped by ZONE instead: the two zones, named explicitly, and no others.
That difference in blast radius is the reason these are two roles rather
than one.
GetHostedZone and ListTagsForResource are how external-dns decides which
records it owns; ListHostedZones and ListHostedZonesByName take no resource
and so are unavoidably on '*'.
Permissions on this role are your decision. This pair is known to work.
